newsitem.title: USA: K-III has higher net on consumer publication strength.
newsitem.headline: K-III has higher net on consumer publication strength.

text.p: K-III Communications Corp., publisher of Seventeen, Modern Bride, New York and Soap Opera Digest magazines, Thursday reported higher results for the fourth quarter and full year.

"Consumer publications, led by Seventeen and Soap Opera Digest, and special interest magazines, including Truckin, Crafts and Horticulture, showed double digit ... growth in revenues and (earnings), driven by increased circulation and advertising," said William F. Reilly, chairman of the board and chief executive officer.

The publishing company, which also produces Channel One, the in-school network, Weekly Reader children's magazine, Nelson Directories and World Almanac, had fourth-quarter profit of $55.3 million, or 32 cents a share, on revenues of $379.4 million. A year earlier it earned $38.8 million, or 25 cents a share, on sales of $284.8 million.

For the year, K-III had a profit of $8 million, or a loss of 27 cents a share, after payment of preferred dividends. In 1995, it had a loss of $75.4 million, or 91 cents share. Sales rose to $1.37 billion from $1.05 billion a year earlier.

"Prospects for 1997 continue to be bright as we expect significant contributions from our core businesses, reap the benefits of the consolidation of recent acquisitions and manage our businesses aggressively," Reilly said.
K-III stock rose 25 cents to $10.75 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
